conventions: A supplied English object pronoun resuming an antecedent that is realized elsewhere is a rule 7 helper on the **verb** that requires it in English, not a discontinuous second realization of the antecedent: `παρέδωκα` → *I delivered them* at 11:2, `πιστεύω` → *I believe it* at 11:18, `ἔκλασεν` → *he brake it* at 11:24, `πίνητε` → *ye drink it* at 11:25. Rule 103 names such a pronoun as rule 7's own case but leaves the carrier open, and its 3JN.1.13 example folds onto the antecedent because there the antecedent is that same verb's own object; where the antecedent belongs to another verb or another verse, the verb that needs the pronoun takes it.

Two **adjacent** source tokens the ASV renders by one English word are one `aligned` unit under rule 39's test, whatever their classes, with the source head on the token that word most directly realizes: `ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς` → *yourselves* (11:13, head on the intensive), `μέρος τι` → *partly* (11:18, head on the noun), `ἄχρι οὗ` → *till* (11:26, head on the adverb), `ὃς ἄν` → *whosoever* (11:27) and `ὡς ἄν` → *whensoever* (11:34) under rule 50. Non-adjacent tokens are not joined: 11:9 gives *neither* to `οὐκ` and leaves the `καί` two tokens in front of it `unrepresented` under rule 65, as rule 41 refuses to join across an intervening word.

A Greek **adverb** the ASV expands into an *in … manner* frame keeps the whole frame as one unit and heads on the word glossing the adverb, *manner* being the generic completion: `ὡσαύτως` → *In like manner* heads on *like* (11:25) and `ἀναξίως` → *in an unworthy manner* on *unworthy* (11:27), as `πρῶτον` → *first of all* heads on *first* (11:18) and `ἱκανοί` → *not a few* on *few* (11:30). Rules 66 and 91 decide it — the corpus spends no *manner* on these lexemes — and rule 99's *what manner of* is a different frame, expanding an interrogative rather than completing an adverb.

An article governing a substantival adjective or the identity pronoun `αὐτός` takes whatever determiner and supplied nominal the ASV writes, and the adjective or pronoun keeps only its own gloss: `τὸ αὐτό` → *the … thing* on the article and *same* on `αὐτό` (11:5), `τὰ … πάντα` → *things* on the article and *all* on `πάντα` (11:12), `Τὰ … λοιπά` → *the* on the article and *rest* on `λοιπά` (11:34). `αὐτός` is not a demonstrative, so rules 38 and 49 do not empty the article in front of it, and rule 60's `αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ` → *that very hour* is the shape. Where the Greek is anarthrous nothing competes and the whole phrase is the adjective's, as `πάντα` → *in all things* headed on *all* at 11:2.
report: Checked all 50 candidate lemma groups and read the full dump end to end, since the table is keyed by source lemma and is blind to `added` units. This chapter has no `added` unit at all (491 aligned, 32 unrepresented, 1 noncompositional), so every supplied English word was checked against its licensing token: *a sign of* (11:10) on ἐξουσίαν, *other* (11:21) on προλαμβάνει, *it* (11:25) on πίνητε, *possible* (11:20) on ἔστιν. In none is the licensing token already spent, so rule 103 does not reach any of them.

No cross-verse split. The groups that looked like one are licensed by the source or by what the ASV wrote: συνέρχομαι's *together* rides inside the verb at 11:17, 11:18, 11:33 and 11:34 and goes to the noncompositional ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό unit only at 11:20, which is rule 106's named contrast and the one verse where that phrase stands; intensifying καί (11:9 and 11:19 empty against 11:6, 11:19, 11:23, 11:25 on *also*) and μέν (11:7 on *indeed* against 11:14, 11:18, 11:21 empty) are rules 65 and 70's English-side test; εἰς τό + infinitive gives *to* to εἰς at 11:33 and the postposed *in* at 11:22, one rule 61 analysis under two ASV phrasings; the article before a substantival adjective at 11:5, 11:12 and 11:34 differs from the anarthrous πάντα at 11:2 on exactly rule 102's test.

Supplied copulas audited as a group are one analysis, differing only by the predicate's class, which the Greek fixes: predicate nominal at 11:3 (noun subject, rule 63), expressed preposition at 11:11 and 11:12 (rule 53), predicate adjective at 11:19 and 11:30, subject pronoun at 11:1 where the predicate is a bare genitive noun. Article-and-possessive is likewise uniform: the article takes the supplied possessive where no genitive pronoun competes (11:5, 11:7, 11:10, 11:15) and is unrepresented where one does (11:4, 11:5, 11:24) — rules 20 and 76, not a split.

BSB 473/483: all ten disagreements are documented convention differences and none is a genuine error. μέν ×3 (rule 70) and ἐάν ×2 (rule 72) are cases the contract says in terms will be reported and are not corrections; the three articles are an articular-infinitive article at 11:21 and 11:22 (rule 61) and the article inside a noncompositional phrase at 11:20 (rule 93, which forbids absorbing it). The one worth naming is 11:22 γάρ: μὴ γὰρ … οὐκ ἔχετε → *What, have ye not* is rule 44's own JHN 7:41 shape, where the supplied interrogative belongs to μή and no English word is left for γάρ. 11:9 καί is rule 65 and its verse note already concedes the joining reading.

Judgments reviewed and deliberately left standing, each already carrying a verse note: 11:4 κατά → *covered*; 11:9 *neither* on οὐκ alone with the non-adjacent καί empty; 11:18 μέρος τι → *partly*; 11:20 *possible* folded onto ἔστιν; 11:25 ὡσαύτως headed on *like*. One unnoted judgment a later reader may want: 11:19 gives *there must* to δεῖ and a bare *be* to εἶναι, where *there … be* on the existential infinitive under rule 96 is also defensible. No edge was changed to improve an aggregate figure.

Four conventions recorded, none of them a restatement: the carrier of a resumptive supplied object pronoun, the joining of adjacent one-English-word pairs against the non-adjacent case, the head of an adverbial *in … manner* frame, and the article standing before a substantival adjective or the identity pronoun αὐτός. No promotion: the two judgments the contract does not name outright are already reachable from rules 103 and 91, and I have no corpus counts for ὡσαύτως or ἀναξίως to carry a rule binding every later chapter.
